Indrajao (Holarrhena antidysenterica) – Uses & Health Benefits 
 
 (Ref: Bhavaprakasa Nighantu) 
 Introduction 
 Seeds of kutaja in Ayurveda are called inderjao and this herb is famous in Ayurveda for treating chronic diarrhoea and dysentery. This herb is arshoghna (treat bleeding piles) and kandhughna (treat irritation of skin) in nature. This herb is bitter and astringent in taste, light and dry in nature and cool in potency. Bark, leaves, seeds and flowers are essential used parts of this plant. 
 This herb is anti-diabetic, anti-fungal, anti-microbial, anti-pyretic, anti-emetic and anti-oxidant in nature. It is used to relieve chronic constipation and also good to treat bleeding piles. It is also an essential remedy for gastrointestinal problems. It is a beneficial herb that helps to boost the immune system and natural process of healing in the body. 
 Plant Description 
 Kutaja is basically a large shrub or glabrous medium sized tree. The Tree is covered with rough greyish or dark-brownish bark. Dark green leaves of the plant are simple, opposite, oval in shape and about 10cm long. White coloured flowers of the plant are less fragrant and about 2-3cm long. Fruits of this plant are cylindrical in shape and paired. Seeds contain numerous light brown coloured seeds that are covered with silky hair. 
 Habitat 
 This plant is basically native to Asian countries and found throughout the India. In India it is wildly distributed in Himalayan regions of higher altitudes of 1100 meters above sea level. It is also found in major regions of Assam and Uttar Pradesh. 
 Names 
 
 Latin name – Holarrhena antidysentrica 
 English name – Conessi tree, conessi bark 
 Hindi name – Kuda, kudaiya 
 Sanskrit name – Kutaja, kalling, inderjava, inderbeeja 
 Telugu name – Kodaga 
 Bengali name – Kurachi 
 Marathi name – Kuda 
 Gujarati name – Kuddo 
 Tamil name – Veppalai, Kodagapal 
 Kannada name – Korachi 
 Malayalam name – Kodgapala 
 Urdu name – Kherva 
 Punjabi name – Kenara 
 Oriya name – Keruan 
 
 Types of Indrajao or Kutaj 
 According to Acharaya Charaka

 Punkutaj/ White – Fruits are large, flowers are white and leaves are soft. Its Latin name is Wrightia tinctoria Br. Its seed is sweet as compared to Krishna variety. 
 Strikutaj/ Krishna – Bark is blackish, fruits are small and flowers are black. Its Latin name is Wrightia tomentosa & Schult.

 The bhavprakash nighantu with elaborated Hindi commentary of Padamshri Prof Krishna Chandra Chunekar and edited by Dr. Ganga Sahay Pandey edition 2010; page number – 73 and verse number – 156. 
 
 According to above – mentioned verse of bhavprakash nighantu inderjao help to pacify tridosha in the body, astringent in taste, sangrahi in nature (cure dysentery) and cool in potency. It is used to treat fever, diarrhoea, bleeding piles, vomiting, leprosy and herpes (visarp). It is also a beneficial herb for treating gout, bleeding disorders, kapha related problems and used to treat excessive pain. 
 Reference:- 
 The bhavprakash nighantu with elaborated Hindi commentary of Padamshri Prof Krishna Chandra Chunekar and edited by Dr. Ganga Sahay Pandey: edition 2010; page number – 73 and verse number – 158.
